samples.summary: The behavior half of the change is never applied: the promote job still has the fall-through `if` chain, so the bug this PR claims to fix is not fixed on this branch
samples.evidence:
The only workflow change in this diff is a new inert text file `docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-workflow.patch`. The live file `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1495-1504` still reads:

```
set +e
node ./scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs "$PR" --promote --require-checks "$REQUIRED"
code=$?
set -e
if [ "$code" -eq 2 ]; ... if [ "$code" -eq 3 ]; ... if [ "$code" -eq 1 ]; ... if [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; ...
```

No `case`, no `*)` default, no redirect to `$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log`, no verdict-line corroboration. So after this PR merges, an exit status outside {0,1,2,3} (127 from a missing binary, 128+signal) still falls through every branch and the step SUCCEEDS silently, and a node crash exiting 1 (SyntaxError / failed import of checks.mjs, set-state.mjs, disclosure.mjs) is still reported as the benign "leaving as draft" — the exact two failures the todo (docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:12-19) says are being closed. This repo has hit this exact pattern before; it is recorded verbatim as a prior panel finding in scripts/agent/rounds.test.mjs:188-191 ("changes ... live only as text inside a committed .patch file under docs/tasks/active/, and are never applied to the real workflow files").
searchedFor: grep mark-ready.mjs in .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml (only the old if-chain at 1496-1504)
grep 'case "$code"' / RUNNER_TEMP in the workflows dir

samples.summary: The new workflow-shape test asserts a `case`/redirect form that does not exist in the repo, so `node --test scripts/agent` is red — and a red verify:self means mark-ready gate 1 can never go green again, stalling the whole loop
samples.evidence: `agent-review-panel.yml handles every mark-ready code, defaults the rest` reads the REAL `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml` (line 330) and then asserts `assert.match(invocation, />\s*"\$RUNNER_TEMP\/mark-ready\.log" 2>&1/)` (line 359), `assert.match(window, /case "\$code" in/)` (363), `/^\s*\*\) echo "mark-ready returned unhandled status \$code"/m` (369) and the `1)`-branch grep (377-387). None of those strings exist in the checked-in workflow (still the `-eq N` chain at 1499-1504), so the test FAILS. The author states this is deliberate (docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:83-86: "fails on purpose ... 13/14 without it"). `scripts/verify-self.mjs:159-161` runs `cd scripts/agent && node --test <every *.test.mjs>` as the `agent:tests` lane, so verify:self is red for this PR and for every PR after it merges. `mark-ready.mjs`'s gate 1 (`ciPassed`, mark-ready.mjs:125-138) requires the CI workflow run to conclude `success`, so with this on main NO agent PR can ever be promoted — the permanent version of the stall the change is meant to prevent. A knowingly-failing assertion must not be merged ahead of the file it asserts about; either land both halves together or gate the assertion on the workflow having been patched.

samples.summary: The grep verdict-string contract is validated against the branch copy of mark-ready.mjs, but the promote job executes the DEFAULT-branch copy
samples.evidence: The promote job checks out the default branch (`.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1466`, `uses: actions/checkout@v4 # default branch — only need the gate script`), so the `grep -qF "Not promoting: one or more gates are not satisfied"` in the patched step is matched against whatever `scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs` is on main, while `mark-ready.test.mjs:389-398` proves the string against the PR-branch copy. Because this change deliberately lands the workflow half by hand at a different time from the script half, the two can be out of step: a maintainer applying the .patch to main while a different mark-ready.mjs (or a reworded verdict line) is on main turns every legitimate exit 1 into "mark-ready CRASHED" → exit 2, reddening the promote job for every not-yet-ready PR. The failure mode is loud rather than silent, hence minor, but the cross-file contract is weaker than the test comment claims.

samples.summary: The 2600-char window that must contain the whole `case` block is only ~700 chars larger than the block it bounds
samples.evidence: `const window = yml.slice(at, at + 2600)` must span from `node ./scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs` through `esac` and the closing assertions. Measuring the patched block in the .patch file gives roughly 1.9 KB, so a couple of added comment lines inside the `case` (the block is already 60% comments) push `esac` and the `*)` default outside the window and the test starts failing with a confusing regex miss rather than a real contract break. Same brittleness class the file's own comment at line 331-333 warns about.

verdict.reason: The live promote job at .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1494-1504 still uses four bare `if [ "$code" -eq N ]` tests with no else: no `case`, no `*)` default, no redirect to $RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log, no grep -qF verdict corroboration. Because a false `if` with no `else` returns 0, an exit status outside {0,1,2,3} (127 missing binary, 128+signal) falls through every branch and the step SUCCEEDS silently; and node's own crash code 1 (SyntaxError / failed import of checks.mjs, set-state.mjs, disclosure.mjs) is reported as the benign "Not all ready-gates satisfied; leaving as draft" — a swallowed failure that leaves a promotable PR as a draft with no page. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: mark-ready is invoked from exactly one place repo-wide (line 1496); no other workflow, composite action or reusable workflow contains a promote exit-code case (the only `*)` occurrences in .github/workflows are a glob in docker-publish.yml:172 and issue-number validation in agent-implement.yml:221); .trusted/ mirrors only scripts/agent, not .github. The corrected block exists solely as unapplied text in docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-workflow.patch:29-47, and the repo's own cross-file contract test (scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:329-399) asserts the case, the `*)` arm, the non-pipe redirect and the verdict needle against the live YAML — assertions the current file cannot satisfy, which the todo (lines 83-86) admits fails on purpose. Real, in-lane (error handling that swallows failures), and blocking.

The test is unconditional (no skip/env guard) and is enumerated by the `agent:tests` lane in scripts/verify-self.mjs:158-162 (`node --test $(find . ... '*.test.mjs' ...)`), so verify:self is red. docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:83-91 confirms the author intends it to fail ("fails on purpose ... 13/14 without it") because the workflow half is parked as an unappliable patch. Consequence chain also verified: mark-ready.mjs:125-140 gate 1 requires the CI workflow run to conclude `success`, and agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1456 gates the promote job on `needs.ci.outputs.conclusion == 'success'`, so a permanently-red CI on main means no agent PR can ever be promoted. That is a broken invariant / core-flow break in the correctness lane (not mere test quality), and nothing guards or skips it.
